subject: Re: Redwood migration & compatibility next steps (OpenAI-compat + hyperscaler comparison)
messages:
From: Samantha Cho <samantha@acmefinancial.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@acmefinancial.com>, platform-team@acmefinancial.com
Date: 2026-03-28T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo - follow-up and next tests

Thanks for the demo today, Marissa - it was helpful to see the low-latency routing and the Dedicated options. A few quick notes from our side and proposed next steps: 

- We want to evaluate realistic migration effort and compatibility against the hyperscaler (GCP AI Platform) we currently run for embeddings + chat. Specifically: API surface parity with our existing OpenAI-compatible calls, SDK swap effort, and any prompt-output diffs.
- Can Redwood run a short compatibility matrix for us (API/response parity, perf on our sample prompts, and token accounting differences)?
- We'd like to schedule a hands-on SDK swap smoke test (one of our engs will swap the client in a staging service). Prefer week of Apr 6.
- Security/compliance asks: confirm default audit log retention and whether keys can be managed via our KMS (we discussed KMS briefly).

Attached: our sample prompt set (see link in the Drive we shared) - I've also attached the short requirements doc we reviewed.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Cho
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Financial Services
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha@acmefinancial.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-28T16:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo - follow-up and next tests

Hi Samantha - great to meet you and Rajiv today, really appreciated the clear migration criteria. Recap + proposed plan below.

Recap (short):
- Primary goals: OpenAI-compatible API path, minimal SDK changes, equivalent output quality, predictable cost/latency vs GCP.
- Constraints: must be able to pin model versions, route by region, and manage keys via your KMS.

Proposed next steps (we can run these as a 2-week Migration Lab):
1) Compatibility matrix (Redwood-run): we'll map OpenAI API calls you use -> Redwood equivalents, run your sample prompts through both Redwood and your current GCP endpoints, and report diffs (response text, token counts, latency).
2) SDK swap smoke test (customer-run, Redwood support): we'll provide a drop-in OpenAI-compatible SDK wrapper and short test harness; your eng swaps the client in staging and runs a 30-minute smoke test. We'll be on the call to triage.
3) Cost/throughput baseline: run a small throughput test (10k tokens/day equivalent) to show per-token cost delta and tail latency at your p95/p99.
4) Security checklist: we'll confirm KMS integration options (Cloud KMS, HSM) and provide the audit-log sample.

Timing: we can start the compatibility matrix the week of Apr 6 and schedule the smoke test Apr 8-10. Does that work for your team?

I'm attaching a short compatibility matrix template and our migration playbook to give structure to the tests. Michael and Dev are looped to lead the technical work.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-compat-matrix.xlsx; redwood-migration-playbook.pdf
From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@acmefinancial.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samantha Cho <samantha@acmefinancial.com>
Date: 2026-03-28T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo - follow-up and next tests

Marissa - thanks. Quick Q on the compatibility matrix: will you include tokenization differences (we use a mix of UTF-8 text and some pre-tokenized pieces for transaction metadata)? Token counts are important for our billing.

Also, can you confirm whether function calling semantics (name/arg mapping) are identical to OpenAI's? We rely on a small controlled set of function calls in prod.

Thanks - Rajiv
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@acmefinancial.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samantha Cho <samantha@acmefinancial.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo - follow-up and next tests

Rajiv - good questions. Short answers up front:
- Tokenization: we'll run your sample prompts through the same tokenizer we expose in the OpenAI-compatible mode and include token-level diffs in the matrix (same token counting algorithm; we'll surface edge cases for pre-tokenized inputs).
- Function calling: Redwood's OpenAI-compatible API supports function/tool calling with the same name/arg semantics; there are minor differences in streaming behavior for very large arg payloads which we'll highlight.

For the smoke test we'll provide:
- A small Node + Python SDK drop-in wrapper (one file) that maps your existing OpenAI calls to Redwood endpoints.
- A test harness that runs your sample prompts and collects p50/p95/p99 latency and token accounting.

Marissa - I'll prep the compatibility matrix runbook and a short script to anonymize sample prompts before we ingest them. Will share by EOD today.

Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Integrations | Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Cho <samantha@acmefinancial.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo - follow-up and next tests

Perfect - thanks, team. Apr 8 at 10am PT works for the SDK swap smoke test; we'll have one of our backend engineers (Priya N.) on the call.

I've uploaded the prompt set and a short sample dataset to the Drive link you shared. I've also attached a short list of our required compliance items (logging retention, KMS SLA).

See you on Apr 8 - please send the calendar invite and the compatibility-matrix template when ready.

Best,
Samantha
